scope: Authored debug-native states of the supporting-line template editor as decided in D89 to D94. Typing is not connected, no template is stored and no player row changes. Not production behaviour, parsing or native accessibility acceptance.
provenanceNote: The commit and APK digest say what produced the captures. Nothing is checked against them (D88).
privacy: Only inspected crops; status strips removed, navigation area and system keyboard retained. Raw hierarchies, logs and screenshots stay private.

capture.renderer: Android Emulator OpenGL ES Translator (llvmpipe (LLVM 20.1.2, 256 bits))

lastVisitRestoredRecordedFields.deviceState: Committed state: DeviceState{identifier=2, name='OPENED', app_accessible=true, cancel_when_requester_not_on_top=false}

verificationLimits: Every text a state draws is compared with what the template reference yields for that state; the native fixture holds authored copy, not a parser.

Whether a text is in view is read from its hierarchy rectangle, the page's scrolling window and the keyboard frame the system reports; hierarchy rectangles are not ink bounds, and a rectangle that touches an edge of the window counts as not in view because the hierarchy cannot tell cut from flush.
Where a page rests with the keyboard open is where the platform puts a focused field (D94); the study scrolls only the end scene, to show the end of the page. Scrolling by hand was not exercised.
Typing, moving the caret by touch, inserting a field and resetting were not exercised; the buttons emit debug events only.
The keyboard is the emulator image's own; its suggestion strip is not part of the study.
TalkBack, focus order, speech and contrast were not exercised.
The inspection sheets show each view below its native size, enough to see any dialog, notice or foreign content but not to read small text; what each view draws is checked from its hierarchy instead.
The keyboard shows the emulator image's own suggestions or, for some views, its tool row; neither is part of the study.
